title: 005 — Databricks, early October 2026: Genie Code CLI, window measures, multi-trigger jobs

005 — Databricks, early October 2026: Genie Code CLI, window measures, multi-trigger jobs

The one idea: Four Databricks releases from 1–6 October change daily data engineering work. There is a terminal coding agent (Genie Code CLI, Beta), rolling and running-total measures in metric views (GA), jobs with up to five triggers (Beta), and Unity Catalog access policies that now hold when other engines read your tables (GA).

Added 2026-10-09 · Released 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-06 by Databricks

1. What it is

Release Status Date In one line
Genie Code CLI Beta 6 Oct A coding agent in your terminal that works with local files and the Databricks CLI
Metric view window measures GA 6 Oct Rolling, cumulative and semiadditive measures defined once in a metric view
Multiple triggers for Lakeflow Jobs Beta 5 Oct Up to five triggers per job, mixed types, each paused on its own
Cross-engine ABAC GA 1 Oct External engines read UC managed tables with ABAC policies, row filters and column masks enforced

2. Why it matters

  • Genie Code CLI brings an agent into the place where pipeline code actually lives: your repo and terminal. It runs under your own identity, so it can only touch what your Unity Catalog permissions allow.
  • Window measures move "7-day active customers" and "running total" logic out of every dashboard query and into one governed definition. Everyone then gets the same number.
  • Multiple triggers remove the common workaround of cloning a job just to run it both on a schedule and on file arrival.
  • Cross-engine ABAC closes a governance gap. Before this, a masking policy protected data inside Databricks, but not when another engine read the same table.

3. How it works

---
title: Window measure — one definition, many queries
---
flowchart LR
    T["Fact table<br/>(orders)"] --> M["Metric view<br/>(YAML measures)"]
    M --> R["t7d_customers<br/>trailing 7 day"]
    M --> C["running_total_sales<br/>cumulative"]
    M --> B["balance<br/>semiadditive: last"]
    R --> Q["Dashboards, Genie,<br/>SQL queries"]
    C --> Q
    B --> Q

A window measure adds a window block to an ordinary measure:

  • order: the field the window moves along, usually a date.
  • range: trailing 7 day, cumulative or current.
  • semiadditive: last: when the date is not in the grouping, return the last value instead of adding values across dates. This is the right behaviour for balances and stock levels.

4. How to use it

Window measure (from the Databricks docs, inside a metric view's measures):

  - name: t7d_customers
    expr: COUNT(DISTINCT o_custkey)
    window:
      - order: date
        range: trailing 7 day
        semiadditive: last

Swap the range for cumulative to get a running total such as SUM(o_totalprice). Use current with SUM(balance) for an account balance that adds up across customers but not across days.

Genie Code CLI (needs Unity Catalog, a supported region and Databricks CLI 1.0.0 or later):

curl -fsSL https://github.com/databricks/genie-code-cli/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
genie --version
cd my-project
genie

On first run, pick a Databricks CLI profile. Windows has a PowerShell installer on the same docs page.

Multiple triggers: in the job's trigger settings, add up to five triggers. For example, a daily schedule plus a file-arrival trigger. Pause each one on its own when you need to.

Cross-engine ABAC: no code change on the reader side. Check the docs for the list of supported external clients, and note that policy enforcement runs on Databricks serverless compute, which is billed.

5. Trade-offs and limits

  • Genie Code CLI is Beta. You cannot choose its model (Databricks picks it). Usage is billed through Unity Gateway, not Genie pricing. It does not share skills or instructions with Genie Code in the workspace. Commands will change.
  • Window measures need metric views. If your team still writes metrics in each dashboard, adopting them is a modelling change, not a toggle. It is worth doing for any KPI quoted in more than one place.
  • Multiple triggers is Beta. Keep critical jobs on one well-understood trigger until it reaches GA.
  • Cross-engine ABAC costs serverless compute for every external read that goes through policy enforcement. Watch the bill if an external engine scans large tables often.
  • Adopt now or wait? Window measures and cross-engine ABAC are GA, so adopt them now. Try Genie Code CLI on a side project. Wait on multi-trigger jobs for production.

6. Where it fits

  • Databricks platform: Unity Catalog, Lakeflow and metric views.
  • Orchestration, quality and governance: triggers, access policies and masks.
  • Pipeline patterns and practices: where shared metric definitions belong.
  • Databricks ai_decide: another recent Databricks SQL addition.

7. Questions to test yourself

  1. Why does a bank balance need semiadditive: last, while a sales total does not?
  2. A team defines "weekly active users" differently in three dashboards. How do window measures fix that?
  3. What did teams do before multiple triggers when a job had to run on a schedule and on file arrival?
  4. Which identity does Genie Code CLI act as, and why does that matter for data access?
  5. Why was a column mask not enough protection before cross-engine ABAC?
